mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above the prior 12-month average predicts a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened discount rates eroding expected future cash flows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in at least 70% of FEDFUNDS-tightening events, or FEDFUNDS change is within ±0.5% of prior month.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS relative to INDPRO indicates strengthening labor market demand, which tends to boost corporate earnings expectations and drive positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically outperforming the 12-month baseline (t-test p > 0.05) in 80% of expansion regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in HOUST above the 5-period moving average signals accelerating industrial demand, which is associated with positive S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of high-HOUST-up moves.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in INDPRO for three consecutive months suggests weakening manufacturing capacity, which is expected to depress corporate earnings and produce negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in over 50% of INDPRO contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months, the policy rate is likely to remain low, supporting equity valuation expansion and a positive S&P 60-day forward return.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns under such triggers are not significantly above the 12-month mean (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both PAYEMS and RSAFS above their 10-period averages suggests robust labor demand and consumer spending, which tends to drive positive S&P 20-day forward returns.
regime_hint: dual labor and consumer demand expansion
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically superior to baseline in 60% of such dual-proxy events.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in GDPC1 (quarterly) accompanied by a decline in CPIAUCSL (monthly) indicates softening aggregate demand, which predicts negative S&P 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such events.

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained period of falling FEDFUNDS for four consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return tends to be positive as investors anticipate future rate cuts and lower borrowing costs.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive in 60% of such four-month declines.
